headline: Dismissed Ansar member hacked to death in Tangail, 2 arrested
summary: The victim was attacked with sharp weapons while returning home from a market in Basail Upazila on Tuesday night.
details: A temporarily dismissed Ansar member named Hanif was hacked to death by attackers in the Bilpara area of Basail Upazila, Tangail, on Tuesday night.
According to locals, the attackers intercepted Hanif while he was returning home from the market, striking him with sharp weapons before fleeing the scene.
Local residents rescued the victim and rushed him to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival.
Following the incident, the victim's wife filed a murder case. Police launched raids in various areas later that night and arrested two suspects.
Law enforcement agencies stated that efforts are ongoing to arrest the remaining suspects involved in the killing.

A temporarily dismissed Ansar member named Hanif was hacked to death by attackers in the Bilpara area of Basail Upazila, Tangail, on Tuesday night.

Local residents rescued the victim and rushed him to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival.

Following the incident, the victim's wife filed a murder case. Police launched raids in various areas later that night and arrested two suspects.

Law enforcement agencies stated that efforts are ongoing to arrest the remaining suspects involved in the killing.

headline_marked: 9 deaths, 1,571 cases: [[Dengue hits yearly high]] in single day
headline: 9 deaths, 1,571 cases: Dengue hits yearly high in single day
summary: Total deaths rise to 130 and cases reach 45,475 this year. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announces a nationwide campaign to combat the spread.
details: Bangladesh recorded its highest single-day dengue deaths and cases so far this year, with nine people dying and 1,571 new infections reported in just 24 hours.
Of the nine deaths, three occurred in Dhaka South City Corporation, while two each were reported in Khulna and Dhaka divisions, and one each in Barishal and Mymensingh.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services, the total number of dengue-related deaths has risen to 130, with reported cases reaching 45,475 this year.
In response, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is set to inaugurate a three-month special nationwide campaign on Saturday, focusing on cleanliness and public awareness.
The Prime Minister emphasized that prevention should not rely solely on government agencies, stressing the importance of keeping homes and surroundings clean to stop the spread.

The campaign will involve local administrations, volunteer organizations, and students, with city corporations coordinating activities in metropolitan areas and deputy commissioners overseeing districts.
Volunteers from the Red Crescent Society, Rover Scouts, BNCC, and students will visit homes and establishments every Saturday to identify and destroy Aedes mosquito breeding sites.
Additionally, the government will run extensive awareness campaigns through television and social media to prioritize prevention and ensure ground-level implementation.
